nodes.question: What does research suggest about the feedback mechanisms of energy apps?
nodes.answer: Research suggests that feedback mechanisms provided through energy apps can encourage user engagement, enhance energy awareness, and facilitate sustainable energy practices.
nodes.paragraph: Among these, energy apps are gaining attention as tools to facilitate household energy management and fos- ter engagement (Valor et al., 2019). Research sug- gests that feedback mechanisms provided through such apps can encourage user engagement, enhance energy awareness, and potentially facilitate sustaina- ble energy practices (Veskioja et al., 2022). The feed- back from the users through these apps can also guide energy providers in refining their operations and ser - vices, including whether the apps features continue to engage users and motivate them to monitor their energy consumption patterns regularly. Despite the growing adoption of these technolo- gies, recent systematic reviews have highlighted both their transformative potential and inherent limita- tions, underscoring the need for more comprehensive exploration of their long-term impacts and scalability (Chatzigeorgiou & Andreou, 2021; Wemyss et al., 2023). A critical shortcoming in existing literature lies in the underrepresentation of the complexity of user interactions with smart energy technologies and the nuanced ways these interactions mediate user percep- tions and engagement (Christensen et al., 2020; Skj Is- vold et al., 2018; Standal et al., 2023).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy management systems|User interface and user experience in ems_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What research gap is identified in the paragraph regarding energy apps?
nodes.answer: The research gap is the lack of understanding of user interactions with energy apps as a medium to facilitate sustainability.
nodes.paragraph: While empiri- cal studies have explored the role of various feedback mediums in influencing energy practices (Hargreaves et al., 2010), there remains a research gap in under - standing user interactions with energy apps as a medium to facilitate sustainability (Valor et al., 2019). Moreover, existing studies predominantly rely on theoretical frameworks or pilot-scale interventions rather than leveraging real-world data from active users (Paneru & Tarigan, 2023). The two main issues in conducting this type of study are the lack of data regarding users engagement with smart energy apps and the limited knowledge to analyse such data. This study addresses this gap by investigating user interac-tions with the Tibber energy app, a digital platform widely adopted by Norwegian households, to explore how such technologies mediate engagement, per - ceptions (Paneru et al., 2023) and energy practices (Paneru & Tarigan, 2023; Simonsen et al., 2022). Norway S position as a global leader in deploying smart energy technologies, characterised by its unique socio-technical context, provides an optimal environ- ment for this inquiry (Korsnes & Throndsen, 2021).

nodes.question: What methodological approach does the study use to understand user experiences with the app?
nodes.answer: The study employs a mixed-methods approach incorporating word analysis, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and exploratory qualitative analysis.
nodes.paragraph: This study employs a mixed-methods approach incorporating word analysis, sentiment analysis, topic modelling, and exploratory qualitative analysis to com- prehensively understand user experiences, perceptions, and engagement with the app. It analyses public user reviews and identifies recurring themes such as user motivations, perceived app value, and reported chal- lenges. These findings contribute to the broader dis- course on the digitalization of energy services, uncover - ing general trends in user engagement and identifying opportunities to enhance app design and functionality to promote energy-conscious practices. Overall, this study is guided by the following research question: RQ How do user interactions with energy appli- cations shape engagement, perceptions, and energy management, and what implications do these interac- tions have for designing user-centric digital energy solutions? nodes.question: What do Wemyss et al. (2023) suggest about the role of energy apps in low-carbon transitions?
nodes.answer: They suggest that energy apps serve as mediators of user engagement and contribute to understanding how digital interfaces influence interactions with energy data and decision-making in the context of social innovations for low-carbon transitions.
nodes.paragraph: Further, Wemyss et al. (2023) emphasise the importance of moving beyond the initial excite- ment around these technologies to understand better the conditions under which they function as social innovations contributing to low-carbon transitions. This perspective underscores the need to study energy apps as mediators of user engage- ment, providing insight into how digital interfaces influence interactions with energy data and inform decision-making. The COVID-19 pandemic has further amplified interest in digital solutions that support sustain- able lifestyles as environmental awareness became a more salient priority for consumers (World Eco- nomic Forum, 2020). Lockdowns and remote work increased reliance on digital tools for managing daily activities, including energy consumption (Gunaratna & Aslam, 2022). This shift created opportunities for digital energy solutions, such as smart energy apps, to play a greater role in household energy manage- ment. Verplanken and Wood (2006) highlight that smart energy technologies, including energy apps, can encourage reflective energy use by providing actionable feedback. Similarly, Sanguinetti et al. (2018) emphasise that user interaction with these technologies can enhance awareness of energy-effi- cient practices.

nodes.question: What do Huijer (2013) and Chalal et al. (2022) contribute to the understanding of energy eco-feedback systems?
nodes.answer: Huijer (2013) observes the effectiveness of tools and their integration with users’ existing practices, while Chalal et al. (2022) highlight the importance of effective visualisation techniques in enhancing user engagement and understanding of energy consumption patterns.
nodes.paragraph: However, Huijer, (2013) observes the effectiveness of these tools and examines how well they integrate with users existing practices and routines. Furthermore, Chalal et al., (2022) conducted a systematic review of energy eco-feedback systems, highlighting the importance of effective visualisation techniques in enhancing user engagement and com- prehension of energy consumption patterns. Recent work by Mosca et al., (2024) maps the landscape of digital interventions to promote sustainability, calling for future studies on effective digital interventions. This study builds on this literature by focusing on how users engage with digital energy platforms, using app reviews as a lens to explore perceptions, evalua- tions, and points of interaction. Relevance of user reviews Analysing user reviews for smart energy apps can offer valuable insights into users perceptions and interactions with these technologies. Particularly, such reviews can highlight how users engage with app features, their awareness of energy feedback, and their perceptions of the app S utility in supporting informed energy decisions. This approach aligns with the growing recognition of energy big data S potential to enhance efficiency by analysing user dimensions (Zhou & Yang, 2016).
